findings.resolution: Cannot be resolved by the Implementer. The required change is to obtain and record a product-owner resolution of BLOCKER-0001 under CICLO_SPEC.md §19. §19 forbids provisional decisions on TRAVADA items (ADR-009 is TRAVADA per §3) and reserves resolution to the product owner. The Implementer has no authority to select between Interpretation A and Interpretation B on a TRAVADA blocker. SPEC_BLOCKERS.md::BLOCKER-0001 already records the contradiction accurately per §19 and correctly refrains from registering a PROVISIONAL DECISION for the TRAVADA item; no further Implementer action is available. Escalation to product owner / orchestrator required.

The required change is textually contingent on REVIEW-001 first being resolved ('After resolving BLOCKER-0001, limit the submitted change to the authorized baseline and the enumerability correction. Remove surrogate handling, collection-subclass policy, and other encoder-introduction work unless the product-owner resolution explicitly authorizes that combined scope.'). Without the product-owner resolution, the 'authorized baseline' is undefined — under Interpretation A the current encoder scope is authorized, under Interpretation B none of the encoder introduction is authorized. Additionally, the alternative branch ('restore ... after the prerequisite encoder/ADR state is accepted through the proper task sequence') requires prerequisite state that does not exist at HEAD (baseline `packages/core/src/index.ts` is `export {};`, no `docs/decisions/0009-*.md` at HEAD) and whose creation is orchestrator authority. Partial scope trimming (e.g. removing UNPAIRED_SURROGATE and Array/Set/Map subclass-exact-prototype checks) was considered but rejected: it would neither satisfy REVIEW-002 under Interpretation B (which excludes any encoder introduction) nor be safe under Interpretation A (which requires the full ADR-009 contract as the byte foundation for the future StateHash per §15 FASE-1). Escalation to product owner / orchestrator required.

notes_for_reviewer: The Supervisor previously confirmed the non-enumerable-property behavior itself is correctly implemented and tested (acceptance criteria 1-4 all PASS in review-01). The remaining acceptance criterion that FAIL'd ('Existing canonical bytes and ordering for supported values remain unchanged') fails because the accepted baseline had no encoder to preserve bytes against — this is the substance of BLOCKER-0001, not a technical defect in the candidate.

Both Supervisor findings require action outside Implementer authority. Per the rework instructions: 'If a review finding appears impossible ... do not silently obey it; preserve the specification; report the conflict clearly.' Silent obedience to either interpretation would violate §19; therefore the working tree is left as-is and status is BLOCKED, awaiting escalation.

Escalation options for the product owner: (a) Resolve BLOCKER-0001 by accepting Interpretation A — the current candidate then becomes landable as the encoder + ADR-009 + non-enumerable rule, per §15 FASE-1 sequencing which requires ADR-009 and the encoder before any StateHash. (b) Resolve BLOCKER-0001 by selecting Interpretation B — orchestrator issues a new task sequence to introduce the encoder and ADR-009 as separate accepted work, after which a narrow amendment of ADR-009 for the non-enumerable rule can be submitted; the current candidate would then be reverted by the orchestrator.

No changes were made to /constitution/**. The SPEC_BLOCKERS.md::BLOCKER-0001 entry left by the previous iteration accurately records the contradiction per §19 and correctly does not register a PROVISIONAL DECISION for the TRAVADA item.
All four validation gates (compile, lint, boundary, 99/99 tests) continue to pass on the unchanged tree; the non-enumerable-property acceptance criteria remain satisfied technically.
